title: Transform query results with the TestData data source

blocks.content:
A transformation runs **after** your query returns and **before** the visualization draws. Instead of rewriting the query, you reshape the frame it produced: reduce a series to a single number, rename and reorder fields, drop rows, join two queries together.

Most transformation tutorials need Prometheus. This one does not. The **TestData** data source ships with every Grafana, so the query half behaves the same everywhere and you can concentrate on the transformation half.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.content: You need edit rights on a dashboard. The first section adds a TestData data source if you have not got one, which needs an administrator — skip it if one already exists.
First, make sure there is something to query.
Open the list of data source types under **Connections**.
blocks.tooltip: TestData generates its own data, so there is nothing to connect and no credentials to enter.

blocks.verify: [data-testid='data-testid Data source settings page Save and Test button']
blocks.tooltip: Grafana creates the data source as soon as you choose a type, with no separate save step.

blocks.content: With a data source in place, build a panel whose results are worth reshaping.
Create a panel and open the panel editor.

steps.tooltip: An unsaved dashboard is enough; nothing here needs saving.
The Add pane opens with the dashboard, and this drops an empty panel onto the canvas.
This opens the editor, where the Queries and Transformations tabs live.
Typing narrows the list to one entry, so the next click cannot land on the wrong data source.
One entry is left after filtering, and this selects it.

blocks.content: Ask for three series, so there is something to reduce.

steps.tooltip: The default Random Walk scenario returns one series, and three makes a transformation's effect visible.
Three random walks should appear in the panel above.

blocks.content: Three series, one query. The tabs below the panel run in the order they are listed: the query fetches, transformations rewrite what it returned, and the visualization draws whatever comes out the end. Nothing you do next changes what Grafana asked the data source for.

blocks.tooltip: The number beside the name counts how many are applied, and it reads zero right now.

steps.tooltip: A drawer opens listing every transformation Grafana ships.
There are more than thirty to choose from, so searching beats scrolling.
Reduce collapses every series to one row per field, using a calculation you choose.

blocks.content: Turn on **Table view** to read the frame the transformation produced.
blocks.tooltip: Three time series have become three rows, each with a name and one calculated value.

blocks.content:
The **Mode** and **Calculations** fields are the two that matter here. *Series to rows* gives one row per series; *Reduce fields* keeps the frame's shape and replaces each field with its calculated value. Change **Calculations** from Max to Mean and the numbers change without the query re-running, because nothing about the query changed.

One transformation is a calculation. Two make a pipeline, and then order starts to matter.
Add **Organize fields by name** after Reduce.

steps.tooltip: The same control, now reading Add another transformation.
Organize fields by name renames, reorders and hides fields.
It operates on the fields Reduce produced, not on the ones the query returned.

blocks.content:
This is the point of the exercise. **Organize fields by name** lists the columns Reduce produced. Put Organize first instead and it would list the three series, and its renames would be thrown away by Reduce a moment later. Each transformation is numbered, so you can drag one above another to reorder the pipeline, or use the eye icon to disable a step without deleting it.

Worth trying next, on the same panel:

- **Filter data by values** — drop rows by a condition instead of filtering in the query.
- **Add field from calculation** — a new field from arithmetic across existing ones.
- **Join by field** — add a second query and line the two frames up on a shared field.

When a transformation is greyed out, that is Grafana saying it cannot apply to the shape of data you currently have. Change the scenario in the **Queries** tab and the list changes with it.
